A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable, and the renamed model, dataset, and renumbered results can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier evaluations and feature ablations in Tables 1 and 4–9, plus the authors' prediction analyses for Helicobacter pylori and SARS-CoV-2.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and case-study results and adds evaluations of sequence-identity controls, alternative splits, structure predictors, and training convergence.

M1.justification: PROVACCINE is renamed VENUSVACCINE, but Section 4 retains the sequence and structure encodings, dual cross-attention, RoPE, attention pooling, and prediction head. AlphaFold2 is evaluated as an alternative structure source; no redesign of the proposed architecture or prediction procedure is specified.

E1.justification: Section 3 broadens the negative-example collection to include experimentally assayed negatives from IEDB and previous studies alongside computationally selected negatives. This changes the represented negative examples within the retained bacterial and viral tasks. Tumor prediction and both pathogen case studies remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds one-hot sequence comparators in Tables 12–14 and SVM predictions to the Helicobacter pylori comparison in Table 16. The principal baseline set remains. Table 1's apparent reassignment of tumor results from VaxiJen2.0 to Vaxi-DL conflicts with Table 6 and Section 5.2.1, so it does not reliably establish another comparator change.

E3.justification: v2 adds a 40% train/test sequence-identity cutoff evaluation, an 8:1:1 bacterial split evaluation, and AlphaFold2-versus-ESMFold settings in Tables 7–11. Section 3's dataset counts increase from 6,817 to 7,216. Appendix C also revises Top-K normalization and describes K as a percentage, although the main text still specifies 30 samples. The original main split and training hyperparameters remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained feature ablations and two case studies, v2 tests sensitivity to sequence similarity, data splitting, and structure predictors; adds one-hot encoding controls; and compares training-loss convergence against vanilla PLMs in Figure 6. These substantially broaden the questions examined about robustness and component utility.

E5.justification: Table 8 newly reports means and standard deviations across five random train/validation/test splits. Both versions retain the main uncertainty procedure described as ten assessments using random 50% test subsets. The new split experiment does not establish an increase in repetitions for the original comparisons.

E6.justification: Many benchmark scores and rankings change: Table 1's Ankh bacterial accuracy changes from 86.2 to 82.3, and ProtBert becomes the highest-accuracy bacterial variant. These are revised results with changed data and incompletely reconciled structure settings, not a demonstrated same-setting deterioration. v2 also adds substantial results and revises tumor ablation entries. The Helicobacter pylori summary and SARS-CoV-2 predictions are retained, allowing for rounding.

T1.justification: Appendix C changes the Top-K formula's denominator from all predictions to the number of top-K predictions. Section 5.3.1 removes the erroneous calculation interpreting 11 × 123 / 1858 as 72.8% recall or probability. The model equations remain mathematically equivalent, and neither version introduces theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The headline dataset-size claim is narrowed from over 9,500 antigens to over 7,000, with 7,216 specified in the introduction. The central contributions—dual-attention prediction, a comprehensive benchmark, and practical post-hoc validation—otherwise retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes performance differences to structural accuracy, recommends AlphaFold2, and notes the shortage of crystal structures. It also qualifies the negative-label selection heuristic and reframes the Helicobacter pylori advantage around enrichment relative to machine-learning baselines. The blanket AlphaFold2 superiority interpretation overlooks exceptions in Tables 9 and 11.

D1.justification: v2's abstract supplies an implementation repository link, whereas v1 only promises release; the old release promise nevertheless remains in Section 5.1. Section 3 adds IEDB eligibility and proteome-sourcing details but omits v1's explicit 100%-identity deduplication description. Hardware and training implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds several PLM-related references, including retrieval-enhanced mutation prediction, VenusFactory, a protein-engineering review, and conditional protein diffusion, while removing SESNet and the cited few-shot-learning study. The overall research positioning remains. ProSST, ProtSolM, and Tan's protein-encoding study are matched publication updates rather than new works.

P1.justification: v2 renames the model and benchmark, revises author affiliations and publication headers, edits introductory and experimental paragraphs, and adds acknowledgments. Dataset construction and the Helicobacter pylori discussion receive localized rewrites. The seven-section main narrative and A–F appendix organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables and the convergence figure, expands feature-ablation tables with one-hot rows, and redraws or resizes existing figures and revises captions. v1 Tables 7–9 become v2 Tables 12–14, while case-study Tables 10–11 become Tables 15 and 17. These retained displays are distinct from the newly added material.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the headline dataset count and erroneous random-selection argument, documents code access, and adds useful sequence-identity and repeated-split evaluations absent from v1. These improve reporting and robustness evidence. The net gain is limited by unreconciled main-versus-ablation results—Ankh bacterial accuracy is 82.3 in Table 4 but 86.2 in Table 12—and an AlphaFold2 superiority interpretation that overstates Tables 9 and 11.
